title: Workshop on Fundamentals of UX
description: The Smt. Kundanben Dinsha Patel Department of Information Technology, CHARUSAT, organized a workshop on “Hands-on Design Thinking & User Experience (UX): Bridging Empathy with Logic” on September 16, 2025, at 628A, A7 Building. Ms. Palak Jadhav, Director – UX at Lemon Yellow LLP, served as the expert speaker and guided 47 participants through key UX fundamentals and modern UI trends. The workshop covered essential principles such as Hick’s Law, Miller’s Law, Fitts’s Law, Jakob’s Law, Cognitive Load, Aesthetic Usability, and more. Students also engaged in hands-on activities using Figma, effectively connecting theoretical concepts with practical application.

title: Workshop - Fundamentals of Network Sniffing
description: Successfully organized a One-Day Workshop on Wireshark for Beginners on 22/09/2025, exclusively for Semester 3 CSPIT-IT students. The session was delivered by Mr. Ankit Bilwankar, Founder of Vivekananda IT Institute, a renowned Trainer and Cyber Security Consultant. Students gained hands-on experience in network fundamentals, packet analysis, and real-time traffic monitoring, which enhanced their understanding of networking concepts and improved their troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.

title: Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning
description: Dr. Jignesh Bhatt from IIIT Vadodara delivered an expert talk on the mathematical foundations of machine learning. The session covered key concepts of linear algebra, probability theory, and regression analysis, highlighting their crucial role in building effective ML models. Participants gained insights into the mathematical underpinnings of prediction and classification techniques in machine learning.

title: Capacity Building Program for Support Staff
description: The Department of Information Technology, CHARUSAT, organized a Capacity Building Program for Supporting Staff on 28th September 2025 at Lab No. 613, A-7 Building, CSPIT. Participants were also introduced to digital and financial literacy, covering basic mobile and internet use, cybersecurity awareness, and government schemes such as Ayushman Bharat and ESIC. The program proved beneficial in enhancing awareness and empowering staff with essential knowledge.

title: Faculty Development Program on Cyber Security & Digital Forensics
description: CSPIT - IT & CE, CHARUSAT, in collaboration with Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), organized a Five-Day Faculty Development Programme (FDP) on “Cyber Security & Digital Forensics” from 1st to 3rd December 2025 and 8th to 9th December 2025. The programme was coordinated by the department faculty members Dr. Martin Parmar and Dr. Priteshkumar Prajapati featured expert sessions delivered by distinguished resource persons Dr. Martin Parmar and Dr. Priteshkumar Prajapati from CHARUSAT and Mr. Dhaval Deshkar, Mr. Varshith Jakkaraju and Mr. Pranjal Upadhyay from RRU. The main contents of FDP are Cyber security, digital forensics, emerging cyber threats, incident response, OWASP Top 10, and MITRE ATT&CK framework. The FDP witnessed enthusiastic participation from faculty members across CE, IT, CSE, and AIML, EC disciplines of CSPIT, DEPSTAR and CMPICA with 20 participants.

title: Workshop - Capture The Flag
description: Successfully organised a Workshop on Hands on Session on : Capture the Flag on 18/09/2025 for 5 semester Students of CSPIT-CSE. The session was delivered by  Dr. Pooja Shah , Assistant Professor and M.Tech Cyber Security Coordinator at Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU) and an Active IEEE member. The session provided hands-on experience in cybersecurity challenges  to solve problems and "capture" digital flags. Key skills include reconnaissance, vulnerability analysis, and digital forensics in a safe, controlled environment.

title: AI Camp
description: The AI Awareness Event at Changa is organized by the Department of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning to spread knowledge about Artificial Intelligence and its practical benefits in farming, healthcare, and education. The event includes a street play, live demonstrations of AI tools, interactive games, and Q&A sessions designed to engage villagers in simple, culturally relatable ways. The aim is to show how AI can become a helpful companion in daily life, empowering rural communities towards a smarter and more self-reliant future.

title: Expert Talk - Next Generation Software Testing
description: An expert talk on “Next-Gen Software Testing: Fundamentals, Tools, and AI Integration” was conducted on 29th September 2025 by Dr. Saurabh Tiwari, Associate Professor & Head, SERL, DA-IICT, Gandhinagar. The session, specifically targeted for 5th semester (3rd year) students of the IT department, covered the fundamentals of software testing, including concepts such as errors, faults, failures, bugs, defects, and verification & validation, along with an overview of static vs. dynamic testing and black box vs. white box approaches with test case generation. Different testing levels such as unit and system testing were discussed, followed by hands-on demonstrations of widely used testing tools like JUnit/Pytest, Mutation Testing, Code Coverage, and Selenium for GUI testing.

title: Endowment Chair Activity by KDPIT with Mr. Shashank Chinchli
description:
The Endowment Chair Activity organized by the Kundanben Dinsha Patel Department of Information Technology (KDPIT), CSPIT, CHARUSAT was conducted from 17 to 19 December 2025 with the objective of enhancing students’ and faculty members’ exposure to industry-relevant cloud technologies. The three-day program featured expert-led sessions on Cloud Computing, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, MLOps, and AI integration with cloud platforms, along with hands-on workshops and career guidance sessions for placement-oriented students.

 As a key highlight, a Cloud-Based Project Competition was organized where students showcased projects in Cloud, Generative AI, Security, and DevOps domains. The top three projects were awarded a total prize money of ₹10,000, encouraging innovation and practical problem-solving. Participants received personalized mentoring, architectural guidance, and constructive feedback from the expert. Additionally, the event facilitated research and industry–academia collaboration discussions for faculty members and research scholars, making the initiative impactful for academic advancement and industry readiness.

title: Expert Talk - AI Projects in the Pharmaceutical Industry
description: The expert lecture on AI Projects in the Pharmaceutical Industry provided valuable exposure to emerging applications of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in the pharmaceutical domain. The lecture highlighted the importance of data-driven decision-making, use of advanced algorithms, and integration of AI tools with biomedical and healthcare datasets. The session enabled participants to gain a comprehensive understanding of the role of AI across various stages of the pharmaceutical lifecycle, including drug discovery, clinical trials, manufacturing, and post-marketing surveillance. The session also emphasized industry-relevant project workflows, current challenges, regulatory considerations, and ethical aspects related to AI adoption in healthcare. Furthermore, it will help students identify potential project ideas, research directions, and career opportunities in the pharmaceutical AI ecosystem.

title: IoT in Smart Manufacturing: Industry 4.0 Applications
description:
The expert talk on Malware Detection proved to be an effective academic activity for Semester 6 students studying Cryptography and Network Security (IT348). It successfully reinforced theoretical knowledge while promoting practical understanding of malware behavior and network defense strategies. Such activities play a crucial role in preparing students for advanced studies, research, and professional roles in cybersecurity. 

 After participating in this event, students were able to: 
 1. Understand core security principles such as the CIA Triad and their role in protecting networked systems.
 2. Identify common malware types and behaviours, including persistence mechanisms and fileless attacks.
 3. Recognize indicators of compromise (IoCs) at both host and network levels.
 4. Analyze real-world attack scenarios and select appropriate defensive and response actions.
 5. Apply incident response concepts, including containment, eradication, and lessons learned.
 6. Appreciate the importance of layered security architectures and proactive threat detection.

 The expert talk made several significant contributions to student learning:
 • Practical Exposure: Students gained hands-on insight into how theoretical security concepts manifest in real cyber incidents.
 • Critical Thinking Development: Scenario-based questions enhanced analytical and decision-making skills.
 • Industry Relevance: Exposure to modern attack techniques aligned academic learning with current cybersecurity trends.
 • Security Awareness: It strengthened awareness of common mistakes in incident handling and the importance of timely response.

description:

The session aimed to enhance students’ understanding of emerging developments, modern techniques, and industry practices in the field of geotechnical engineering .

The expert lecture was delivered by Mr. Himanshu Kotak, Geotechnical Engineer and Founder, C-Phi Consult Pvt. Ltd., Ahmedabad who provided valuable insights into recent advancements in geotechnical investigations, ground improvement techniques, and contemporary challenges faced in geotechnical engineering practice. A total of 22 students, along with faculty members, actively participated in the session. The interactive discussion and enthusiastic participation reflected keen interest among students in learning about evolving geotechnical engineering practices. The expert talk contributed significantly to enriching students’ technical knowledge and professional outlook.
